A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research despite the shortened title. Their main text, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments on five models and call-graph prompting experiments, with detailed results in Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds three evaluated models, a sliding-window intervention and quantitative error analyses.

M1.justification: The task generator and call-graph comment methods remain unchanged. Section 3.2 adds a small inference adaptation for hosted GPT-4o models: an opening quote is appended to the prompt instead of enforcing string output through constrained decoding.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four synthetic Python retrieval tasks using synthetic distractors and HumanEval filler functions. Additional models, window configurations and error analyses do not introduce new datasets or task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated model set expands from five to eight, adding DeepSeekCoder-6.7B-base, GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o while retaining all earlier models. The additions participate in both retrieval comparisons and call-graph prompting comparisons, including v2 Tables 5–6 and 11–13.

E3.justification: v2 adds Mistral window-size conditions of 2048 and 8192 alongside the default 4096, evaluated on the one-step task at 8k with five distractors. It also introduces error-category measurements and Levenshtein distance. Existing context lengths, distractor counts, accuracy@3 evaluation and sampling hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's brief manual error inspection becomes quantitative analyses of distractor answers, partial concatenations and edit distances in v2 Section 3.5.2 and Appendix B. The new window-size intervention in Figure 5 directly probes the architectural explanation previously inferred from comparisons between models. Existing comment-template, direction and depth analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The forward-reference comparison gains explicit 95% confidence intervals when v1 Table 6 becomes v2 Table 2. Both versions already describe normal-approximation intervals assuming independent samples, ten generations per prompt and a fixed dataset-generation seed; no increase in repeated runs is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive model, window-size and error-analysis results, plus detailed names-only prompting scores. It corrects summary means: Mistral's one-step mean changes from 61.5% to 82.0% despite unchanged per-context scores. Existing interval values also change. Pooled prompting results cover an expanded model set and are not directly comparable performance gains. Some retained-model curves change without an explained protocol revision: Figure 8's StarCoderBase-7B concatenation result with both comments at 8k changes from approximately 26% to 9%.

T1.justification: The task definitions, forward-reference and spread definitions, and generation algorithm retain their mathematical substance. Neither version introduces theorems or proofs; the added use of Levenshtein distance is an empirical measurement rather than a theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The central retrieval benchmark and prompting contributions remain. v2 broadens the stated evaluation contribution to proprietary models, qualifies the abstract's ordering penalty as affecting many models, and reframes practical prompting recommendations as an investigation. The headline sliding-window and prompting-benefit claims are retained.

C2.justification: v2 develops more differentiated interpretations of spread and errors and explicitly acknowledges exceptions to the forward-reference trend. Section 6 adds substantive boundaries concerning recursion, branching, reused functions, random identifiers and decoder-only architectures. Prompt modifications are explicitly exploratory and are not recommended over alternatives such as fine-tuning.

D1.justification: v2 specifies exact GPT checkpoint versions and the hosted-model quote-prefix workaround. Appendix prompt examples now identify key/value functions, and the full-sentence example adds the final assert. Sampling hyperparameters, hardware, compute estimates and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds DeepSeek-Coder and GPT model citations and a focused discussion of attention explanations and mechanistic interpretability, including Elhage, Hernandez and Brinkmann. It further explains its relationship to PVR and CoderEval, while retaining the original related-work categories and central positioning.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title, adopts author-year citations, promotes incorrect responses into a separate subsection and appendix, and rewrites portions of the discussion and limitations. The main section sequence and most task and method exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different typography and page layout. v2 adds the window-size figure and error-analysis tables, expands many plots with new models, moves the forward-reference table into the main text with highlighted exceptions, restructures the prompting summary table, and consolidates per-model prompting figures into task-wise grids.

improvement.justification: The controlled window-size experiment, stronger-model comparisons, corrected summary means and more explicit limitations improve validation and interpretation. These gains are tempered by reporting inconsistencies: revised call-graph curves are not reconciled with retained per-model aggregates in Table 11, and the new edit-distance interpretation assumes an unexplained 11-character answer length despite Section 3.1's task description. The net improvement is therefore qualified.
